title: Holiday accrual for irregular-hours and part-year workers (12.07%)
summary: Working Time Regulations 1998 regulations 15B to 15F (inserted by SI 2023/1426): for leave years starting on or after 1 April 2024, irregular-hours and part-year workers accrue holiday at 12.07% of hours worked in each pay period, up to 28 days a year. Great Britain only. It does not apply to workers with regular hours.

title: Northern Ireland: no 12.07% accrual or rolled-up holiday pay regime
summary: The Great Britain 2023 changes (12.07% accrual and rolled-up holiday pay for irregular-hours and part-year workers) were not made in Northern Ireland. Holiday is 5.6 weeks a year under the Working Time Regulations (NI) 2016, pro rata for part-time and irregular work, paid when taken. No NI legislation authorises rolled-up holiday pay, and the CJEU (Robinson-Steele, 2006) held it incompatible with the Working Time Directive, so it should not be used.

title: Protection of wages: lawful deductions (Employment Rights Act 1996, Part II)
summary: A deduction from wages is only lawful if required or authorised by statute, by a contract term given or notified in writing beforehand, or by the worker's prior written consent. Retail workers: deductions for cash shortages or stock deficiencies are capped at one-tenth of gross wages on a pay day.

title: Protection of wages: lawful deductions (Employment Rights (NI) Order 1996, Part IV)
summary: Northern Ireland equivalent of ERA 1996 Part II: deductions need a statutory basis, a written contract term notified beforehand, or prior written consent. The same one-tenth retail cap applies.

title: Minimum wage: deductions and payments for uniform, equipment and training
summary: National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015: deductions or payments for the employer's own use and benefit, or for expenditure connected with the job such as uniform, equipment or training, reduce pay for minimum wage purposes, even if lawful under the wage protection rules. Time spent on required training is working time. Check every pay reference period.

title: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018
summary: Controllers need a lawful basis and must give privacy information. Where one business processes personal data for another, Article 28 requires a written contract with set processor terms.
